what_happened: A command denial written as Bash(*<word>*) matches the whole command text, so it refuses a read that only names the word. On card 001 the console seat's read-only grep of console/uv.lock, searching for the Micro-Manager binding's name, was refused by such a pattern in console/.claude/settings.json. The seat used the Grep tool instead, which no command pattern reaches, and did not reword the command. Check 53 refuses a Bash denial that names a reading utility, on the assumption that every other Bash pattern blocks running and not reading; this pattern blocks both. Judged here: no proposal. The over-block errs in the safe direction. Check 53's purpose, that a seat can always read, still holds through the Read, Grep and Glob tools, which it guarantees stay open. Narrowing a hardware-name denial to spare reads would loosen a guard that stands beside safety, for the sake of convenience.
cue: a command pattern meant to block running also blocks reads that merely name the guarded word
lesson: Keep the dedicated read, search and glob tools guaranteed open, and have seats use them when a command pattern over-blocks instead of rewording the command.
